correctness.rationale: Proof: global domination iff every part is met. For each part with singleton, select a distinct partner missing only that part; mark one vertex per other part. The exact E=N-k account yields E>=s(r-2)+(r-s)(m-s)/2. At m>=3r-6 this entails E>=r(r-2), including integrality at s=r-1; explicit r-hub construction gives equality. At m>=3r-4, all s<r have E>r(r-2), forcing s=r; equality forces precise hub sizes and all other singleton classes. Distinct hub omissions make the labelled injection product a bijection. The included standard-library exhaustive tests and arithmetic checks replay successfully but are not substitutes for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The already published multipartite construction and r<=3 classification are excluded from novelty. The new result is the matching upper bound for all r>=4 with sufficiently large arbitrary part sizes, plus uniqueness of the structure and exact count of all labelled maximum partitions in a stronger range. Full primary manuscript inspected, and available semantic research searches returned no covering claim; absolute priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: The sufficient size conditions are not claimed sharp.
The full conjecture for smaller parts remains unresolved.
An unindexed or unpublished proof of the whole conjecture could cover the exactness portion; analogous prior enumeration was not identified but cannot be ruled out.
The introductory 2020 paper was not read in full; its scope is not a decisive blocker for this exact multipartite conjecture.

value.rationale: A motivated theorem for an explicit infinite tail of Conjecture 54, allowing any number r>=4 of unequal parts, with a new structural argument and a complete classification/count of maximum partitions. This is not a routine recomputation of a known lower bound: the missing upper bound is proved and all equality cases are characterized.
